extracted.intended_audience: writers, art-critics, and cultivated literary readers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles about creating and judging literary and artistic work (especially fiction, poetry, and memoir), with emphasis on imagination, mystery, the role of criticism, and formal effects such as rhyme and dramatic situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of autobiography/egotism
rubrics_metrics.description: In literature mere egotism is delightful. I like [memoirs] for their form, just as much as for their matter. Whenever we come across it ... we cannot but welcome it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Autobiography and personal confession attract and fascinate readers; the personal 'secrets' of the writer can charm and hold attention (examples: Cicero, Balzac, Rousseau, Pepys). Treat the mode/form of memoir as equally important as content; candid self-revelation is a literary virtue rather than a vice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave the artist alone / limits of criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: Why should the artist be troubled by the shrill clamour of criticism? Why should those who cannot create take upon themselves to estimate the value of creative work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid intrusive, explanatory criticism that disturbs artistic creation. Critics who cannot create risk misunderstanding and vulgarising art; the artist's freedom to create without explanatory intrusion is a value to be protected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits of explanation in criticism
rubrics_metrics.description: If a man’s work is easy to understand, an explanation is unnecessary. . . . And if his work is incomprehensible, an explanation is wicked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should resist over-explaining: for transparent works, commentary is redundant; for obscure works, forced explanations do damage. Criticism should recognise when interpretation is needless or harmful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve mystery in art
rubrics_metrics.description: We have so few mysteries left to us that we cannot afford to part with one of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mystery and the sense of the unknown are artistic resources; criticism that strips away mystery (by explaining or demystifying) impoverishes art. Cultivate and protect inscrutability where it serves imaginative effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art purifies life by selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Art... purify it for us, and give to it a momentary perfection. The imagination... should, as it were, purify it for us, and give to it a momentary perfection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artistic work should exercise choice and selection: rather than reproducing life wholesale, shape and refine it into an aesthetically purified, momentarily perfect representation. Evaluate works by how well they select and elevate aspects of life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagination works best in solitude
rubrics_metrics.description: The imagination spreads, or should spread, a solitude around it, and works best in silence and in isolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creative writing and imaginative work flourish when the artist is allowed solitude and silence; environments of chatter or relentless criticism are detrimental. Encourage conditions for focused, solitary imaginative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestiveness for fiction is more important than fact
rubrics_metrics.description: To be suggestive for fiction is to be of more importance than a fact. To be suggestive for fiction is to be of more importance than a fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing fiction, prioritize its capacity to suggest, evoke, and inspire imaginative extensions over mere factual accuracy. A detail that serves suggestion and imaginative possibility is superior to dry factuality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancient/ideal absence of critics
rubrics_metrics.description: In the best days of art there were no art-critics... No irresponsible chatter disturbed him. He was not worried by opinions. By the Ilyssus there were no silly art congresses...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The historical ideal presented is art produced free from institutionalised criticism and modern journalistic chatter; assess whether contemporary critical practices are constraining or corrupting artistic production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper use of rhyme as a spiritual element
rubrics_metrics.description: Rhyme... in the hands of the real artist becomes not merely a material element of metrical beauty, but a spiritual element of thought and passion also... Rhyme... became in Robert Browning’s hands a grotesque, misshapen thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In poetry, formal devices like rhyme should do spiritual and suggestive work (enhancing mood and idea). Avoid mechanical or inappropriate uses of rhyme that produce grotesque, comic, or discordant effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic situation and character creation as primary merits
rubrics_metrics.description: He will be remembered as a writer of fiction... His sense of dramatic situation was unrivalled... Considered from the point of view of a creator of character he ranks next to him who made Hamlet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate poetic or literary work by its capacity to create convincing dramatic situations and living characters; dramatic imagination and character-making may outrank purely musical or formal accomplishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not vulgarise heroes / respect in biography
rubrics_metrics.description: Formerly we used to canonise our heroes. The modern method is to vulgarise them. Cheap editions of great men are absolutely detestable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biographers and memoirists should avoid the modern tendency to trivialise or vulgarise great figures; retaining dignity and a respectful distance can be an artistic choice. Evaluate life-writing for whether it honors or cheapens its subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art as technical re-creation (form, colour, material skill)
rubrics_metrics.description: Through form and colour he re-created a world... Panel and marble and linen canvas became wonderful as his brush swept across them; and life seeing her own image, was still, and dared not speak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess craftsmanship: mastery of materials (form, colour, media-specific techniques) and the capacity to re-create life with technical skill are central criteria. Look for precision of medium-specific techniques and the ability to instill life into form.
